title: Louis Armstrong's visit and its effect on local players
summary: The Armstrong band played set showcase numbers, only Edmond Hall varied much, and local players copied it badly.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What about Armstrong coming over there? Do you think that he was doing much improvising or the band was doing much improvising?

Uh, no, that, that's the trouble. They were playing, uh, showcase stuff. Um, I don't blame them. They've got to live. They've played their jazz. But, uh, they did have this bad effect on, uh, a lot of the local boys. Um, um, Um, and, uh, Armstrong just seemed to play the same, uh, tunes, the same solos. And, uh, I'm afraid, uh, a lot of the, uh, local boys just tried to do the same sort of thing, which was pretty ridiculous.

How did, uh, the, uh, whatchamacallit, uh, the, uh, the whole band, with the piano player and the trombone player and all the rest of them do the same thing? Or would some of them get off a little more?

In the Armstrong band? Yeah. Yes, um, Edmund Hall was the only one who was, uh, doing much, uh, in the front line. Billy Kyle, uh, uh, would vary it a bit, but not much. They had their set numbers and their set way of playing them and they played them. It was, uh, they were a great crowd pleaser and, uh, drew a lot of, uh, huge audience.
It's, uh, it's a pity, especially with a fellow like them. It's a pity.
